1bcb027c5553.en: Add Gaussian noise $\varepsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\sigma^{2}\boldsymbol{I})$ to the input; after a Taylor expansion, the approximate objective gains an extra term:

b40b0fa0aa4f.zh: 這一項懲罰輸入梯度的大小，讓輸出對輸入小擾動不敏感。
b40b0fa0aa4f.en: This term penalizes the size of the input gradient, making the output insensitive to small perturbations of the input.

2a83281b11d8.zh: 真的算一遍：兩種懲罰對照
2a83281b11d8.en: Let's actually work it out: the two penalties side by side

a9c6b3f04948.en: For the simple linear model $\widehat{y}=w x$:

f2d12528b218.zh: 兩者相等。一般來說，$\alpha\approx 2\sigma^{2}$ 時效果類似。
f2d12528b218.en: The two are equal. In general, the effects are similar when $\alpha\approx 2\sigma^{2}$.

50dfc0ed546e.zh: 你可能以為 weight decay 只是「讓權重變小」。反轉在：它真正的效果是把激活函數推離飽和區。大權重會讓 sigmoid/tanh 進入平坦的兩端，網路變得過度非線性；weight decay 讓網路保持在接近線性的區域，泛化更好。
50dfc0ed546e.en: You might think weight decay just "makes the weights smaller". The twist: its real effect is to push the activation functions away from their saturation regions. Large weights drive sigmoid/tanh into their flat tails, and the network becomes overly non-linear; weight decay keeps the network in a nearly linear region, so it generalizes better.

75eb981e6371.zh: 把神經網路想成音響。大權重像把音量轉到極大，喇叭進入失真區；weight decay 把音量拉回合理範圍。輸入雜訊像房間裡有一點背景噪音，好的音響不會因為小噪音就輸出爆音。
75eb981e6371.en: Think of a neural network as a sound system. Large weights are like cranking the volume all the way up, so the speakers go into distortion; weight decay brings the volume back to a reasonable level. Input noise is like a little background noise in the room: a good sound system doesn't blast out a pop just because of a little noise.

cbe785adc131.zh: 第一個誤解：weight decay 只適用於線性迴歸。錯，它廣泛用於神經網路。第二個誤解：輸入雜訊與 weight decay 完全等價。錯，只在 Taylor 一階近似下類似。第三個誤解：權重越小，模型一定越弱。錯，適度的 weight decay 通常讓測試表現更好。
cbe785adc131.en: First misconception: weight decay only applies to linear regression. Wrong, it is widely used in neural networks. Second misconception: input noise and weight decay are exactly equivalent. Wrong, they are only similar under a first-order Taylor approximation. Third misconception: the smaller the weights, the weaker the model must be. Wrong, a moderate amount of weight decay usually makes test performance better.

54c47da9afec.zh: KP-12 的 L2 特徵收縮公式，就是式 (51) 的基礎。
54c47da9afec.en: KP-12's L2 eigen-shrinkage formula is the basis of Eq. (51).

f1dd8605764e.zh: KP-15 的 early stopping 與 weight decay 在二次近似下等價。
f1dd8605764e.en: KP-15's early stopping is equivalent to weight decay under a quadratic approximation.

5dd71671ff12.zh: KP-16 的 dropout 也透過類似「子網路平均」來降低 variance。
5dd71671ff12.en: KP-16's dropout also lowers variance through a similar "averaging over subnetworks".

fcc5b61bd828.zh: Weight decay 直接懲罰大權重；輸入雜訊透過 Taylor 展開間接懲罰輸入梯度；兩者都讓模型更平滑、對擾動更穩健。
fcc5b61bd828.en: Weight decay penalizes large weights directly; input noise, through a Taylor expansion, indirectly penalizes the input gradient; both make the model smoother and more robust to perturbations.

036941cd5ba5.zh: 一句話收尾： 限速器與好懸吊，兩種做法都讓車子不會因小顛簸就失控。
036941cd5ba5.en: In one sentence: a speed limiter and good suspension: both keep the car from losing control over a small bump.

c7e0711aebd1.zh: 教授祕笈：Early Stopping 與 Weight Decay 的等價性（式 (54)–(59)）
c7e0711aebd1.en: Professor's Secret Notes: The Equivalence of Early Stopping and Weight Decay (Eqs. (54)–(59))

d14d53cfacb5.zh: 同學，early stopping 是最簡單的正則化：練到驗證誤差最低就停。這一節告訴你一個很優美的結論：在二次近似下，「早點停止」跟「多一點 weight decay」其實是同一回事。
d14d53cfacb5.en: Folks, early stopping is the simplest kind of regularization: train until the validation error is at its lowest, then stop. This section gives you a really elegant result: under a quadratic approximation, "stopping a bit earlier" and "a bit more weight decay" are actually the same thing.

89fd76f87663.zh: 煮麵時，你不可能煮越久越好。煮太少會硬（欠擬合），煮太多會爛（過擬合）。Early stopping 就是「撈起來的時機」；而 weight decay 則像「一開始就少放一點麵」。兩者最後都讓碗裡的麵軟硬度差不多。
89fd76f87663.en: When you cook noodles, longer is not always better. Too little and they're hard (underfitting); too much and they turn to mush (overfitting). Early stopping is "the moment you fish them out", while weight decay is like "putting in a few less noodles to begin with". Either way, the noodles in the bowl end up about equally firm.

7c9c7d7dde63.en: Let gradient descent start from the origin with learning rate $\eta$; after $t$ iterations:

3401aa782049.en: then taking logarithms and a Taylor approximation gives:

37d6f705d8e1.en: Suppose $\eta=0.1$. If you stop at $t=10$ steps, the corresponding weight decay strength is roughly:

760adb8b9fa2.zh: 也就是說：「訓練 10 步就停」大約等價於「用 $\alpha=1$ 的 weight decay 一直訓練到收斂」。少訓練 = 更強的正則化。
760adb8b9fa2.en: In other words: "stopping after 10 training steps" is roughly equivalent to "training all the way to convergence with weight decay $\alpha=1$". Less training = stronger regularization.

1033d13bd672.zh: 你可能以為 early stopping 不夠「數學」。反轉在：它跟 L2 正則化在二次近似下是等價的。這不是湊巧，而是因為兩者都在限制權重能長到多大。
1033d13bd672.en: You might think early stopping isn't "mathematical" enough. The twist: under a quadratic approximation it is equivalent to L2 regularization. That's no coincidence; it's because both limit how large the weights can grow.

a7a73d32cd84.zh: 把權重想成「債務」。訓練越久，債務累積越多（權重變大）。Early stopping 是「少借一點時間」；weight decay 是「每期多還一點本金」。兩者最後都讓債務總額控制在類似範圍。
a7a73d32cd84.en: Think of the weights as "debt". The longer you train, the more debt piles up (the weights get bigger). Early stopping is "borrowing for a shorter time"; weight decay is "paying back a bit more principal each period". Either way, the total debt ends up kept in a similar range.

7f84add734a8.zh: 第一個誤解：early stopping 只看訓練誤差。錯，它看驗證誤差。第二個誤解：停止得越早，模型一定越好。錯，太早會欠擬合。第三個誤解：式 (59) 是精確等價。錯，它是 Taylor 近似，只在二次近似與小學習率下成立。
7f84add734a8.en: Misconception one: early stopping only looks at the training error. Wrong, it looks at the validation error. Misconception two: the earlier you stop, the better the model is guaranteed to be. Wrong, stop too early and you underfit. Misconception three: Eq. (59) is an exact equivalence. Wrong, it is a Taylor approximation, valid only under the quadratic approximation and with a small learning rate.

fc00d34f136c.zh: KP-10 的 Err 回升曲線，給出 early stopping 該停的理論位置。
fc00d34f136c.en: KP-10's rising Err curve gives the theoretical point where early stopping should stop.

3119fd9b919a.zh: KP-14 的 weight decay 是這裡的對照組。
3119fd9b919a.en: KP-14's weight decay is the comparison group here.

1a0f430f4114.zh: KP-11 把正則化講成 $J+\alpha\Omega$ 的一般框架。
1a0f430f4114.en: KP-11 presents regularization as the general framework $J+\alpha\Omega$.

0d881760605e.zh: Early stopping 用「少訓練」來限制權重大小；在二次近似下，它等價於一個對應強度的 weight decay。
0d881760605e.en: Early stopping limits the size of the weights by "training less"; under a quadratic approximation, it is equivalent to weight decay of a corresponding strength.

3af53ae472e2.zh: 一句話收尾： 煮麵別煮爛，訓練別訓過頭；早停與 weight decay，一體兩面。
3af53ae472e2.en: In one sentence: don't overcook the noodles, don't overtrain the model; early stopping and weight decay are two sides of the same coin.

2189a9c73940.zh: 教授祕笈：Bagging、Dropout、BatchNorm 與章節總結（式 (60)–(69)）
2189a9c73940.en: Professor's Secret Notes: Bagging, Dropout, BatchNorm, and Chapter Summary (Eqs. (60)–(69))

a7ce00d9119c.zh: 同學，來到最後一節。前面講了切分、誤差分解、正則化；這一節介紹三種實務上常用的正則化/降低 variance 技巧：bagging、dropout、batch normalization。它們的共通目標是讓模型更穩定、更泛化。
a7ce00d9119c.en: Folks, we've reached the last section. So far we've covered data splitting, error decomposition, and regularization; this section introduces three regularization / variance-reduction techniques commonly used in practice: bagging, dropout, and batch normalization. Their common goal is to make models more stable and better at generalizing.

ad4040bdd3a1.zh: 想像你要預測明天會不會下雨。你可以問一個專家（單一模型），也可以問一群專家並投票（bagging）。為了避免專家們互相抄答案，你讓他們各自只看到部分資料（bootstrap）或在討論時偶爾閉嘴（dropout）。最後你還把大家的意見先做標準化（batch norm），讓比較公平的投票更容易進行。
ad4040bdd3a1.en: Imagine you want to predict whether it will rain tomorrow. You can ask one expert (a single model), or ask a group of experts and take a vote (bagging). To keep the experts from copying each other's answers, you let each of them see only part of the data (bootstrap), or have them occasionally keep quiet during the discussion (dropout). Finally, you also standardize everyone's opinions first (batch norm), so that a fairer vote is easier to hold.

de549e405bd6.en: Bagging: train $h_{1},\dots,h_{k}$ on $k$ bootstrap samples, then average:

5164b9794397.en: Assuming the models' error covariance is $c$ and the variance of a single module is $s$, then:

9830cc495f90.zh: Dropout：訓練時以機率 $p$ 保留神經元，測試時乘 $p$ 來近似子網路平均。
9830cc495f90.en: Dropout: during training, keep each neuron with probability $p$; at test time, multiply by $p$ to approximate the average over subnetworks.

c07cf8a91bb4.zh: BatchNorm：對 mini-batch 每個特徵標準化：
c07cf8a91bb4.en: BatchNorm: standardize each feature over the mini-batch:

a2756cdcef6e.zh: 真的算一遍：Bagging 的 variance 降低
a2756cdcef6e.en: Let's actually compute it: bagging's variance reduction

a1774dea445f.en: If the models are completely independent ($c=0$): $\operatorname{Var}=1/10=0.1$.

67086109a4f8.en: If the models are highly correlated ($c=0.8$): $\operatorname{Var}=0.1+0.9\times 0.8=0.82$.

1cd38958f3dd.zh: 差很多！這就是為什麼 bagging 要讓模型「多樣化」，例如用不同子集或不同特徵。
1cd38958f3dd.en: Huge difference! That's why bagging needs the models to be "diverse", e.g. by using different subsets or different features.

46b40595e90d.zh: 對於 dropout，若 $p=0.5$，測試時輸出乘 $0.5$ 來模擬「訓練時只有一半神經元存活」的平均效果。
46b40595e90d.en: For dropout, if $p=0.5$, the output is multiplied by $0.5$ at test time to simulate the average effect of "only half the neurons surviving during training".

e3539bf4f61e.zh: 你可能覺得 dropout 就是「隨機關神經元，讓網路變弱」。反轉在：dropout 其實在訓練大量不同的子網路，測試時的縮放是在做這些子網路的幾何平均。它不是變弱，而是讓網路學會更穩健的特徵表示。
e3539bf4f61e.en: You might think dropout just means "randomly switch off neurons and make the network weaker". The twist: dropout is actually training a huge number of different subnetworks, and the scaling at test time is taking the geometric mean of these subnetworks. It doesn't make the network weaker; it makes it learn more robust feature representations.

6835b97a06be.zh: 把 bagging 想成「投資組合」。如果你把錢分散在 10 支低相關股票上，整體波動會遠小於單一股票；但如果 10 支股票都同漲同跌，分散就沒用。Dropout 像「每次只讓部分球員上場練習」，讓每個球員都能獨當一面。
6835b97a06be.en: Think of bagging as a "portfolio". If you spread your money over 10 weakly correlated stocks, the overall volatility is far smaller than a single stock's; but if all 10 stocks rise and fall together, diversifying is useless. Dropout is like "letting only some of the players onto the field at each practice", so that every player can hold their own.

438cb39a6a9a.zh: 第一個誤解：bagging 一定降低 bias。錯，它主要降低 variance。第二個誤解：dropout 測試時也要隨機關神經元。錯，測試時全部打開並乘 $p$。第三個誤解：BatchNorm 的主要作用是減少 covariate shift。錯，後續研究顯示它主要平滑損失地形、穩定梯度。
438cb39a6a9a.en: Misconception one: bagging always lowers bias. Wrong, it mainly lowers variance. Misconception two: dropout also randomly switches off neurons at test time. Wrong, at test time all of them are switched on and multiplied by $p$. Misconception three: BatchNorm's main role is to reduce covariate shift. Wrong, later research showed that it mainly smooths the loss landscape and stabilizes gradients.

17104b9325c6.zh: KP-2、KP-3 的 variance 與 covariance 是式 (64) 的基礎。
17104b9325c6.en: The variance and covariance from KP-2 and KP-3 are the foundation of Eq. (64).

907a5bc86ffc.zh: KP-9 的交叉驗證也利用「平均多個估計」來降低變異。
907a5bc86ffc.en: KP-9's cross-validation also uses "averaging several estimates" to reduce variance.

94fac6b0fb22.zh: KP-11–KP-15 的各種正則化，與這裡的技術互補。
94fac6b0fb22.en: The various regularizers in KP-11 to KP-15 complement the techniques here.

617ff34639a2.zh: Bagging 透過平均多個多樣化模型來降低 variance；Dropout 線上訓練大量子網路並以縮放近似平均；BatchNorm 穩定每層輸入分布，讓訓練更順暢。
617ff34639a2.en: Bagging lowers variance by averaging several diverse models; dropout trains a huge number of subnetworks online and approximates their average by scaling; BatchNorm stabilizes the input distribution of each layer, so training goes more smoothly.

ee7923d7ec67.zh: 一句話收尾： 多個臭皮匠要夠不一樣才有效；隨機缺席與標準化，是深度學習裡讓隊伍穩定的兩招。
ee7923d7ec67.en: In one sentence: a crowd of ordinary folks only beats the genius if they're different enough from each other; random absences and standardization are the two moves in deep learning that keep the team steady.
